chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a Muslim man who died and had a Christian mother, and he also had a wife and Muslim children. He said: “If his mother accepts Islam before his inheritance is divided, she is given one-sixth.”

I said: “What if he has no wife, no child, and no Muslim heir who has an allotted share in the Book, while his mother is Christian and his relatives are Christians among those who would have a share in the Book if they were Muslim? For whom is his inheritance?” He said: “If his mother accepts Islam, then all of his inheritance belongs to her. If his mother does not accept Islam, but some of his relatives from among those who have a share in the Book accept Islam, then his inheritance belongs to that relative. If none of his relatives accepts Islam, then his inheritance belongs to the Imam.”

key_terms.سَهْمٌ فِي الْكِتَابِ: a fixed share established in the revealed legal rule
key_terms.لِلْإِمَامِ: belonging to the Imam as the final legal recipient

ai.seo_question: Who inherits a Muslim’s estate if his Christian mother or Christian relatives accept Islam after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out inheritance rulings for a Muslim deceased whose close relatives are non-Muslim, especially when a Christian mother or Christian kin later accept Islam. It clarifies that conversion before division of the estate can establish entitlement, and that if no qualifying relative becomes Muslim, the estate returns to the Imam.
